header.title: OpenBooks
header.heroAlt: OpenBooks: the library with categories and the first books, including Gugel, Wattjes and Vandepitte
header.label: Historical building literature
header.tagline: Trade books nobody prints any more, free to open in your browser
header.desc: Anyone renovating or assessing an existing building wants to know how it was built back then. OpenBooks puts scanned building books from 1670 to the 1960s online: pick a book, leaf through the original pages and zoom into the drawings.

meta.description: Free online library of scanned historical building books: Wattjes, Gugel, Vandepitte, Zwiers, Bosboom and old Dutch concrete codes. Browse and zoom into the original pages, no account needed.
meta.title: OpenBooks — OpenAEC Foundation

collection.alt: Bookshelf with Staalconstructies, Handboek Houtconstructies, Gewapend Beton Voorschriften and Bosboom's Cort onderwys, among others
collection.title: The standard works you can no longer find second-hand
collection.desc: Wattjes on walls, foundations, window frames, stairs and roofs, Gugel's theory of form, Vandepitte on structural analysis, steel by Potma and De Vries, timber by Zwiers and the 1950 concrete code. Every book with author, year and page count.

find.alt: Category Constructie selected: five volumes of Wattjes' Constructies van Gebouwen
find.title: The right book in two clicks
find.desc: Pick a subject, such as construction, steel, timber or codes, and you only see those books. Or type a title or an author in the search box.

read.alt: Reader with Wattjes volume 4, page 60 of 205: text on door frames with a drawing of a draught door
read.title: Leaf through the original, page by page
read.desc: Every book opens in a calm reader with the real scans. Turn pages with the arrows or your keyboard, type a page number or click the progress bar to jump straight to a chapter.

zoom.alt: Gugel's Architectonische Vormenleer at 250 percent: arches and brick bonds in detail
zoom.title: Every detail of the drawing in sharp view
zoom.desc: Zoom up to five times with the scroll wheel or the buttons and drag the page wherever you want. That way you can read dimensions, pointing and profiles on the old plates.

classic.alt: Cort onderwys vande vyf colommen by Symon Bosboom from 1670, with the Ionic column and its dimensions
classic.title: Three centuries of building knowledge side by side
classic.desc: From the treatise on the five orders of columns by Dordrecht's city stonemason Symon Bosboom from 1670 to Vandepitte's methods of analysis from the 1960s. Useful for restoration, and a pleasure to browse.

whatsnew.label: New in 2026
whatsnew.title: A proper reader for every book
whatsnew.desc: This year OpenBooks got its own website with a reader that shows every scanned page, with zoom, panning and jumping to a page.

books.a: The reader holds twelve books with over 2,300 pages in total: five volumes of Wattjes' Constructies van Gebouwen, Gugel's Architectonische Vormenleer, Vandepitte's Berekening van Constructies I, Staalconstructies by Potma and De Vries, Zwiers' Handboek Houtconstructies, the 1950 reinforced concrete code, Bosboom's Cort onderwys from 1670 and a book on panel doors. GitHub holds even more scans, such as the other volumes of Wattjes and Vandepitte, Bernoulli's Vademecum and the 1974 concrete code.

install.q: Do I need to install anything?
install.a: No. Open open-books.open-aec.com in your browser and pick a book. No account needed.

price.a: Nothing. OpenBooks is free and open source; the website and scripts are licensed under the LGPL-3.0.

format.q: What file format are the scans in?
format.a: Every page is a separate image (PNG or JPG) in one folder per book on GitHub. You can view and download them there, page by page or as the whole collection.

systems.q: Which systems does it run on?
systems.a: In any modern browser on Windows, macOS and Linux. It works best on a computer with a mouse; the site itself is in Dutch.

practice.a: Yes, for work on existing buildings: you see how walls, foundations, frames, stairs and roofs used to be built and calculated. Note: the codes in the collection are historical and no longer apply today.

ocr.q: Can I search the text of the books?
ocr.a: Not yet. The search box currently searches by title and author. Text recognition (OCR), so you can search for words in the pages and copy text, is planned.

rights.a: As far as can be traced, the books are free of rights. That is sometimes hard to establish. If you think a book is still under copyright, report it on GitHub and we will remove it.

contribute.a: Please do. Scan a rights-free building book and submit the pages as a contribution on GitHub, or open an issue with a tip for a book that belongs here.

react.desc: The library and the reader are a single web page built with React, without a build step.

git.desc: All scans live in a Git repository, one folder per book, so every change can be traced.

static.title: Static site
static.desc: No server code or database: the pages load straight from the repository.

actions.desc: A workflow automatically publishes every change to open-books.open-aec.com.

python.desc: Small scripts number and rename the scanned pages per book.

license.desc: Open licence for the code; the books themselves are, as far as can be traced, free of rights.
